claims.statement: As of an April 2026 FDA update, BPC-157 was removed from the FDA's Category 2 'significant safety risks' bulk drug substances list after the original nominators withdrew their nomination; this is a procedural change, not new safety data. BPC-157 now appears under 'bulk drug substances nominated but withdrawn' and remains an unapproved new drug not on any FDA-permitted compounding list (503A or 503B), so compounding it still carries unresolved regulatory and safety uncertainty. At its July 23-24, 2026 meeting, the FDA's Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee (PCAC) voted to recommend that FDA include BPC-157 (with KPV, TB-500, MOTS-c, Epitalon, and Semax) on the 503A Bulks List; this recommendation is advisory and non-binding — BPC-157 remains an unapproved new drug not on any FDA-permitted compounding list unless and until FDA acts on it.

context.population: humans exposed to compounded BPC-157 products

extractedEvidence.quote: BPC-157: Compounded drugs containing BPC-157 may pose risk for immunogenicity for certain routes of administration and may have complexities with regard to peptide-related impurities and active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) characterization. FDA has identified no, or only limited, safety-related information for the proposed routes of administration. Therefore, the agency lacks sufficient information to know whether the drug would cause harm when administered to humans.

extractedEvidence.quote: BPC-157 is officially being removed from the Category 2 list (the banned list for substances with significant safety risks). This removal was triggered because the original nominators formally withdrew their nominations. Because BPC-157 was removed from Category 2, but not yet added to Category 1, it meets none of the criteria. The FDA has officially announced its intention to consult the Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee (PCAC) on July 23, 2026, regarding the potential inclusion of BPC-157 (acetate and free base) onto the approved 503A list.

claims.statement: A literature review describes broad preclinical interest in BPC-157 but emphasizes scarce human studies and the need for human-oriented studies to establish therapeutic and toxic profiles. An independent 2025 systematic review of 36 studies found only 1 human clinical study (a small retrospective case series, with 7 of 12 patients reporting relief for >6 months after intra-articular knee injection) and stated that no clinical safety data were found for BPC-157.

independently corroborated 2026-08-29 by STAT News: a University of Utah Health physician states BPC-157 should not be used by humans absent proper trials; nearly all existing evidence traces to one Croatia-based research group (Sikiric et al.); a 2015 human trial registered on clinicaltrials.gov was withdrawn before external review with no peer-reviewed results ever published

Regulatory-status drift resolved 2026-08-29: FDA removed BPC-157 from the Category 2 significant-safety-risk list in April 2026 after nomination withdrawal (procedural, not a safety finding); BPC-157 remains an unapproved new drug not on any permitted compounding list, and at the July 23-24, 2026 PCAC meeting the committee voted to recommend BPC-157 for the 503A Bulks List (advisory, non-binding; awaiting FDA action). Claim bpc157-regulatory-compounding-risk-001 and its sourceRefs were rewritten and re-verified against a live re-fetch of the FDA page plus an independent legal/regulatory commentary source (Holt Law) rather than re-affirming the original stale FDA-page-only citation; next reviewer should re-check the live FDA page again ahead of/after the July 2026 PCAC meeting, since the outcome of that meeting may change status again.
